scores.reason: Joint scaling laws for batch size and learning rate, but appears LLM-focused; no small-scale CNN experiments; lacks optimizer-specific hyperparameter rules (warmup, momentum, averaging).
Completely unrelated: LLM hallucination detection, not training dynamics.
Three-term scaling law addresses critical batch size, but context is LLM pretraining; no small-scale CNN or short-horizon regime demonstrated; lacks concrete hyperparameter scaling rules.
Critical batch size analysis for GANs with TTUR, not CNNs; gives complexity results but no concrete hyperparameter scaling rules for lr, momentum, warmup, or averaging.
Theoretical proof that optimal batch size exists (rational function relationship), but purely mathematical analysis without empirical validation on small-scale tasks.
Pool-based active learning batch selection; unrelated to supervised training batch size scaling.
Adaptive batch size learning for SGD on strongly convex functions; too narrow in scope (no neural networks, no modern optimizers).
Pure LLM work on μP parametrization with vocabulary scaling; no small-scale CNN or transferable batch-size scaling rules.
Dynamic batch size adaptation coupled to learning rate, but proposes adaptive algorithm (variance-based) rather than explicit scaling rules; experimental scope unclear.
Pure LLM pretraining scaling study; excluded as token-scaling without transferability to CNN short-horizon regime.

Gives concrete scaling rules: B ∝ ε (SGD), B ∝ 1/(1-m) for momentum; addresses momentum coefficient scaling; empirical across multiple tasks including CIFAR; directly addresses equivalence of lr decay and bs increase; meets all rubric criteria.
LLM pretraining in infinite-data limit; critical batch size evolves with token budget; no small-scale CNN or short-horizon experiments.
Learning rate schedule theory only; does not address batch size scaling or joint hyperparameter rules.

Derives optimal batch size and learning rate growth schedules to minimize SFO complexity; includes both theory and validation; but experimental scale not specified—unclear if includes short-horizon (≤2000 steps) or CIFAR-scale datasets.

Concrete scaling rule: multiply lr by 1/√2 when doubling batch size; principled framework for Adam and normalized SGD; finite-sample equivalence proof for SGD; but no mention of small-scale CNN experiments or short-horizon validation.
Temporal graph learning evaluation methodology; unrelated to supervised training batch size scaling.

Analyzes SGDM with dynamic lr and batch size schedules (constant vs. increasing, decaying lr with increasing bs); shows convergence hierarchy; includes empirical validation; addresses momentum but experimental scale (CIFAR vs. LLM) not specified.

Concrete momentum scaling rules: η_Polyak^crit ∝ B(1-ρ), η_Nesterov^crit ∝ B^β(1-ρ); critical batch size phase diagram; one-pass regime (short training); but uses power-law kernel regression analytically, not empirical CNN validation; lacks warmup and averaging rules.

Derives concrete analytical lr-to-batch-size rules: linear scaling (SGD), square-root scaling (Adam) from random matrix theory; applicable to neural networks; but purely theoretical without empirical small-scale CNN experiments.

Automated lr scheduler for large-batch training with epoch budget; emphasizes warmup strategy for constrained steps; but proposes automatic algorithm rather than explicit scaling rules (e.g., warmup_fraction ∝ 1/B); no momentum, ghost BN, or EMA ablations shown.
